steps.title: Relate x and y
steps.narration: Because x varies inversely as y, their product xy equals a constant k.

steps.title: Find the constant
steps.narration: Convert two and a half to five over two and multiply by two to get k equals five.

steps.title: Find x when y is 4
steps.narration: Divide the constant five by the new value y equals four to get one and one quarter.

teach.title: Set up the inverse law
teach.narration: Inverse variation means as y gets larger, x gets smaller in the same ratio, so x equals a constant k divided by y.

teach.title: Make k the subject
teach.narration: Multiply both sides by y so we can calculate the constant product k from the first pair of values.

teach.title: Find the constant k
teach.narration: Change the mixed number two and a half into the improper fraction five over two, then multiply by two to get five.

teach.title: Find x at y equals 4
teach.narration: Now put k equals five and y equals four into x equals k over y, giving five quarters, or one and a quarter.

teach.title: Check the product
teach.narration: Double check by multiplying one and a quarter by four, which gives five again. So x equals one and one quarter.

steps.title: Angle in a semicircle
steps.narration: RS is a diameter, so angle R T S on the circumference is ninety degrees.

steps.title: Find angle RST
steps.narration: Subtract ninety degrees and twenty five degrees from one hundred and eighty degrees to get angle R S T equals sixty five degrees.

steps.title: Apply alternate segment
steps.narration: By the alternate segment theorem, the angle between the tangent and chord T R equals sixty five degrees.

teach.title: List what is given
teach.narration: First read what the question gives us: R S is a diameter, T lies on the circle, and angle T R S is twenty five degrees.

teach.title: Use angle in a semicircle
teach.narration: Any angle at the circumference standing on a diameter is a right angle, so angle R T S inside triangle R T S is ninety degrees.

teach.title: Find the third angle
teach.narration: The three angles in triangle R T S add up to one hundred and eighty degrees, so subtract ninety and twenty five to leave sixty five degrees for angle R S T.

teach.title: Use alternate segment theorem
teach.narration: By the alternate segment theorem, the acute angle x between the tangent at T and chord T R equals the angle subtended by T R in the opposite segment, which is angle R S T.

teach.title: Read the value of x
teach.narration: Therefore the acute angle x is sixty five degrees.

steps.title: Identify base and height
steps.narration: The two shorter sides of a right-angled triangle meet at ninety degrees, so they are the base and height.

steps.title: State the area formula
steps.narration: Use half times base times height for the area of a triangle.

steps.title: Calculate the area
steps.narration: Multiply half by four and five to get ten square centimetres.

teach.title: Identify the shorter sides
teach.narration: In a right-angled triangle, the longest side is always the hypotenuse. That means the two shorter sides, four and five centimetres, form the right angle.

teach.title: Write the area formula
teach.narration: Because the two shorter sides are perpendicular to each other, one serves as the base and the other as the height.

teach.title: Substitute four and five
teach.narration: Put four centimetres for the base and five centimetres for the height into the formula.

teach.title: Evaluate the area
teach.narration: Half of four is two, and two times five gives ten square centimetres.

steps.title: State sector formula
steps.narration: A sector's area is the angle over three hundred and sixty degrees times pi r squared.

steps.title: Substitute given values
steps.narration: Put in fifty degrees for the angle, twenty two over seven for pi, and six for the radius.

steps.title: Cancel and simplify
steps.narration: Cancel thirty six top and bottom, then multiply five by twenty two over seven to get one hundred and ten over seven square centimetres.

teach.title: List what is given
teach.narration: Read the angle fifty degrees, radius six centimetres, and pi equals twenty two over seven from the question.

teach.title: Write sector area formula
teach.narration: A sector is a fraction of the full circle, so multiply the full circle area pi r squared by the angle fraction over three hundred and sixty.

teach.title: Substitute the numbers
teach.narration: Replace theta with fifty, pi with twenty two over seven, and r with six.

teach.title: Simplify before multiplying
teach.narration: Reduce fifty over three hundred and sixty to five over thirty six, and evaluate six squared as thirty six.

teach.title: Cancel and finish
teach.narration: The thirty sixes cancel out cleanly, leaving five times twenty two over seven, which is one hundred and ten over seven square centimetres.

steps.title: Read the gradient
steps.narration: Read the coefficient of x from y equals minus four x plus two to get gradient minus four.

steps.title: Use parallel gradient
steps.narration: Parallel lines share the same gradient minus four, so substitute the point two comma three.

steps.title: Find the y-intercept
steps.narration: Multiply minus four by two to get minus eight, then add eight to both sides so c equals eleven.

steps.title: Rearrange to zero form
steps.narration: Move minus four x and eleven to the left side to get y plus four x minus eleven equals zero.

teach.title: Find the given gradient
teach.narration: In y equals m x plus c, the number in front of x is the gradient, so the given line has gradient minus four.

teach.title: Keep the same gradient
teach.narration: Two lines are parallel only when they have the exact same slope, so our new line also uses m equals minus four.

teach.title: Write the new equation
teach.narration: Start with y equals minus four x plus c, where c is the unknown y-intercept we need to find.

teach.title: Substitute the point
teach.narration: Since the line passes through two comma three, put x equals two and y equals three into the equation.

teach.title: Add eight to both sides
teach.narration: Add eight to both sides to isolate c, giving c equals eleven, so y equals minus four x plus eleven.

teach.title: Rearrange and check
teach.narration: Add four x and subtract eleven from both sides to write y plus four x minus eleven equals zero. Checking at two comma three gives three plus eight minus eleven equals zero.

steps.title: Use sine area formula
steps.narration: Use half times the two sides times sine of the included angle sixty degrees.

steps.title: Substitute values
steps.narration: Put in twelve root three for the area, eight for P Q, q for P R, and root three over two for sine sixty.

steps.title: Solve for q
steps.narration: Simplify the right side to two q root three, then divide both sides by two root three to get q equals six centimetres.

teach.title: List what is given
teach.narration: Read the two sides meeting at P, eight and q, the included angle sixty degrees, and the area twelve root three.

teach.title: State the sine area rule
teach.narration: When we know two sides and the angle between them, the triangle area equals half a b sine C.

teach.title: Substitute known values
teach.narration: Substitute twelve root three for the area, eight and q for the sides, and the exact value root three over two for sine sixty degrees.

teach.title: Simplify the right side
teach.narration: Multiply half by eight to get four, then divide by two to leave two q root three.

teach.title: Divide to find q
teach.narration: Divide both sides by two root three so the root three cancels out, leaving q equals six centimetres.

steps.title: Set up the chain rule
steps.narration: Let u equal the inner expression two x plus one, so y becomes u cubed.

steps.title: Differentiate outer and inner
steps.narration: Differentiate u cubed to get three u squared, and differentiate two x plus one to get two.

steps.title: Multiply and substitute
steps.narration: Multiply the two derivatives together and replace u with two x plus one to get six times two x plus one all squared.

teach.title: Name the inner bracket
teach.narration: Because two x plus one is raised to a power, we use the chain rule. Call the inside bracket u.

teach.title: Differentiate the outer power
teach.narration: Bring the power three to the front and reduce the power by one, giving three u squared.

teach.title: Differentiate the bracket
teach.narration: Now differentiate the inside expression two x plus one with respect to x, which gives two.

teach.title: Multiply the derivatives
teach.narration: The chain rule multiplies the outer derivative by the inner derivative.

teach.title: Substitute u back
teach.narration: Multiply three by two to get six, and put two x plus one back for u, giving six times two x plus one squared.

steps.title: Integrate sine x
steps.narration: The integral of sine x is minus cosine x, since differentiating minus cosine x returns sine x.

steps.title: Integrate the constant
steps.narration: The integral of the constant two with respect to x is two x.

steps.title: Combine and add k
steps.narration: Combine both terms and add the integration constant k to get minus cosine x plus two x plus k.

teach.display: ∫ (sin x + 2) dx = ∫ sin x dx + ∫ 2 dx
teach.title: Split into two integrals
teach.narration: We can integrate a sum term by term, so handle sine x and two separately.

teach.title: Integrate sine x
teach.narration: Remember that the derivative of cosine x is minus sine x, so going backwards, the integral of sine x is minus cosine x.

teach.title: Integrate two
teach.narration: Integrating a constant multiplies it by x, because the derivative of two x is two.

teach.title: Add constant and check
teach.narration: Always add the arbitrary constant k for an indefinite integral. Differentiating minus cosine x plus two x plus k returns sine x plus two, confirming minus cosine x plus two x plus k.

steps.title: Find the mean
steps.narration: Add the four numbers to get sixteen and divide by four to get a mean of four.

steps.title: Sum squared deviations
steps.narration: Subtract four from each value, square the differences to get four, one, one, and four, and add them to get ten.

steps.title: Find the variance
steps.narration: Divide the sum ten by the four data values to get a variance of five over two.

steps.title: Take the square root
steps.narration: Take the square root of the variance to get the standard deviation, root five over two.

teach.title: State the SD formula
teach.narration: Population standard deviation is the square root of the average squared distance from the mean.

teach.title: Calculate the mean
teach.narration: First find the mean by adding all four scores, giving sixteen, and dividing by four to get four.

teach.title: Find each deviation
teach.narration: Subtract the mean four from each number to see how far each value sits from the middle.

teach.title: Square and add
teach.narration: Square every deviation so negatives become positive, giving four, one, one, and four, which sum to ten.

teach.title: Divide by n
teach.narration: Divide the sum ten by four, the number of values, and reduce the fraction to five over two for the variance.

teach.title: Take the square root
teach.narration: Finally take the positive square root of the variance to obtain the standard deviation, the square root of five over two.

steps.title: Convert mixed number
steps.narration: Convert three and two thirds into the improper fraction eleven over three.

steps.title: Multiply the top
steps.narration: Cancel two with six to leave three, then multiply across the top to get fifty five over twenty seven.

steps.title: Multiply the bottom
steps.narration: Cancel three into fifteen and two into four, leaving eleven over two hundred and seventy.

steps.title: Divide the fractions
steps.narration: Flip the bottom fraction and multiply, cancelling eleven into fifty five and twenty seven into two hundred and seventy to get fifty.

teach.title: Convert the mixed number
teach.narration: Before multiplying fractions, change three and two thirds into an improper fraction by multiplying three by three and adding two to get eleven over three.

teach.title: Multiply the numerator
teach.narration: Now work out the top product separately so the expression stays clean.

teach.title: Cancel and multiply top
teach.narration: Divide the two in the numerator and the six in the denominator by two, then multiply across to get fifty five over twenty seven.

teach.title: Multiply the denominator
teach.narration: Next simplify the bottom product by cancelling common factors before multiplying large numbers.

teach.title: Cancel and multiply bottom
teach.narration: Three divides into fifteen five times and two divides into four two times, leaving eleven over five times two times twenty seven, which is eleven over two hundred and seventy.

teach.title: Flip and multiply
teach.narration: Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal. Fifty five divided by eleven is five, and two hundred and seventy divided by twenty seven is ten, giving five times ten equals fifty.
